content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a framework for Chinese named entity recognition that utilizes dependency trees in a tree LSTM framework and then feeds the hidden representations into a standard chain-CRF layer. Experiments on four Chinese NER benchmarks show promising results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The presentation is in general clear
- The motivation to capture long-range dependency makes sense for the studied task

Weaknesses:
- This submission studies a specific NLP task on a specific language, making it more appropriate to be submitted to a standard NLP venue
- Technical novelty seems limited (see clarification below)
- Lack of practical utility: baselines built on standard BERT models consistently outperform the variant with the presented tree-LSTM on all benchmarks if gold-standard POS tags or dependency trees are not used, which are not available in practice anyway
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall the presentation seems clear. However, there seems to be huge room for improvement in terms of literature review.

Similar ideas to inject dependency trees in NER or other sequence labeling tasks have been explored, e.g. this paper (and a few others that I can't immediately recall for now):
- Jie & Lu. Dependency-Guided LSTM-CRF for Named Entity Recognition. EMNLP 2019.

The more generic design of tree-structured LSTM has been studied for years, and even in the same year of 2015 there have been many papers simultaneously presenting very similar ideas:
- Tai et al. Improved Semantic Representations From Tree-Structured Long Short-Term Memory Networks. ACL 2015.
- Le & Zuidema. Compositional distributional semantics with long short term memory. SEM 2015.
- Zhu et al. Long short-term memory over recursive structures. ICML 2015.

As a result, it seems difficult for this submission to catch much attention from the ICLR attendees.

I'd suggest the authors try to submit this paper to an NLP venue after exploring some different properties (e.g., superiority in some specific domains) against BERT-based models over more modern architectures such as modifications over self-attention as presented by the EMNLP 2018 best paper:
- Strubell et al. Linguistically-Informed Self-Attention for Semantic Role Labeling. EMNLP 2018.
content.summary_of_the_review: Clearly written but lack of novelty or practical utility, while being more suitable for an NLP venue

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a novel way of combining tree structures with LSTMs, for the task of Named Entity Recognition for four Chinese-language datasets. The authors describe how bidirectional LSTMs work with their dependency parsing: from root to leaf for the first pass, and from leaf to root for the second pass.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- Novel method that presents a new, truly bidirectional way of information flow in an LSTM

Weaknesses:
- Results are somewhat weak and do not achieve SoTA for the Tree-LSTM
- Results remain mixed for BERT with Tree-LSTM
- There is no discussion of prior work for tree structures and LSTM (and there are quite a few papers to cite)
- Unclear takeaway from the paper given results

Additional Notes:
- Please proofread the paper for spelling mistakes
- In Table 4, add the references next to the model names instead of listing them in the caption
- In Table 4, only highlight in bold the best results
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is not clearly written and needs work -- the message of the paper remains unclear. The quality and novelty are good, and there are sufficient hyperparameter details for reproduciblity.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the method is novel and well thought out, the results are mixed, and call into question whether tree structures help with Named Entity Recognition. There needs to be a proper discussion of the results, and in this light, a discussion of the contribution of the paper. In this state, the paper does not provide sufficient proof that the effectiveness of the method is verified. In addition, there is no discussion of how this proposed tree-LSTM compares to existing Tree-LSTM methods.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a bidirectional recursive LSTM model for named entity recognition.
The model can effectively leverage syntax information and other prior knowledge (e.g., POS and arc labels) to facilitate the NER task.
The experiment result demonstrates that the proposed model achieves the best performance over baseline systems.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
1. The motivation to convert chain-style LSTM into tree-based to capture the non-linear dependency is reasonable.
2. The experiment results verify the model's effectiveness, and the ablation study indicates the usefulness of different modules. (e.g., POS, arc label)

Weakness: 
1. Lack of novelty. The idea of encoding dependency parse trees via recursive LSTM to facilitate NER, to me, is trivial or say not novel, so far, which has been widely explored in [1] and [2]. More broadly, the exploration of tree-like LSTMs is well studied, such as the recursive LSTM [3,4], Nary-Tree LSTM and Childsum-Tree LSTM [5].

2. It is unclear what the association is between Lattice LSTM and the model proposed in this paper.
Lattice LSTM aims to utilize existing word vocabulary to help improve NER, which is unrelated to this paper's core idea.

3. This model claims that the model is able to capture long-range dependency to help NER, while the Experiment Section did not give prove it with evidence.

4. Missing very important references [5].

[1] Dependency-Guided LSTM-CRF for Named Entity Recognition. EMNLP. 2019.

[2] Leveraging linguistic structures for named entity recognition with bidirectional recursive neural networks. EMNLP 2017.

[3] Dynamic pooling and unfolding recursive autoencoders for paraphrase detection. NIPS 2011.

[4] Recursive deep models for semantic compositionality over a sentiment treebank. EMNLP, 2013.

[5] Improved Semantic Representations from Tree-Structured Long Short-Term Memory Networks. ACL. 2015.
content.summary_of_the_review: The novelty and model architecture of this paper are not impressive, and the experiment result did not fully reflect the ideas claimed in the Introduction Section.

content.title: Tree Structure LSTM for Chinese Named Entity Recognition
content.abstract: In this paper, we remodel the bi-directional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) network for Chinese Named Entity Recognition (NER). We convert LSTM from chain-like structure into tree structure which is fixed to the dependency parsing tree of the sentence. The new structure model can fully leverage the syntax information of the sentence and has the capability of capturing long-range dependencies. In addition, we use dependency parsing label embedding to improve the performance of our approach. Experimental studies on four benchmarking Chinese NER datasets have verified the effectiveness of our approach.
